# Lagos Free Zone calls for shift from trading to manufacturing

![](https://cdn.thenationonlineng.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12095900/Lagos-605x340.jpeg)

Lagos Free Zone, Nigeria’s first private special economic zone, centrally located in Lagos State and promoted by Tolaram, has called for a shift from trading with Nigeria to manufacturing in Nigeria, urging Indian businesses to deepen their investments in local manufacturing and develop export-oriented value chains that can serve Nigeria, the wider African market, and global destinations.

Managing Director, Lagos Free Zone, Adesuwa Ladoja, who spoke at the Nigeria-India Export Summit, themed: “Driving Sustainable Export Growth through Trade, Investment and Market Access between Nigeria and India,” in Lagos, said that the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and India provided a strong foundation for a new phase of economic cooperation, with investment, manufacturing, and value addition playing a greater role in future trade.

She noted that while energy would remain an important part of the relationship, sustainable growth would require both countries to look beyond commodity exchange and build businesses that create products and value locally.

She said: “For many businesses, the most important step is to move from selling in Nigeria to making in Nigeria. That shift is already underway, and this is where the next wave of value will come from. Investing here, building a strong local presence, and developing a supply chain that manages inputs and outputs locally is critical to sustainable success”.

She explained that Nigeria’s market size, natural resources, and access to the wider African market, combined with India’s manufacturing and technological capabilities, presented opportunities to develop competitive production and export value chains.

She added that Lagos Free Zone provides an integrated platform with the infrastructure and connectivity to support manufacturing, trade, and exports, enabling businesses to create competitive products while retaining more value within Nigeria.

She said: “Our message to Indian companies is simple: make in Nigeria, for Nigeria, for West Africa, and for the world, including the US and European markets. At Lagos Free Zone, we are ready to help turn that opportunity into factories, jobs, and exports. We believe the future of Nigeria-India trade should be measured not only by how much we exchange, but by how much value we create together”.

In his welcome address, the Host of the Nigeria-India Export Summit, Puneet Arora, explained that the summit provided an opportunity to strengthen commercial ties between Nigeria and India and to explore opportunities in trade, infrastructure, agriculture, market access, and investment. He noted that sustainable export growth would depend on stronger supply chains, investment, and lasting commercial relationships between businesses in both markets.
